success_patterns: Verbatim archive hits ('CATEGORY | clue | answer') were copied exactly, even when the answer is a pun-like phrase that does not look like the clue's slot type ('this type of job' -> 'high pressure'). The category header (WEATHER WORDS & PHRASES) explains the pun.

Clues built on a unique anchor (Khartoum, Tynwald, Jasper Johns' flag, 'Some of Me') were answered with the entity that owns the anchor, with the type taken from the clue's noun (nation, island, painter, daughter). The agent did not echo the anchor or the memoir title.

Clue fragments with stage directions or extra description ('Jon of the Clue Crew peers down between the cymbals', 'Georgia guy, flag-fashioning pop painter') were solved by matching the factual core and ignoring the filler.

For a caption-style clue whose picture is missing ('The dipper seen here is to be used with this sticky substance'), the agent used the standard collocation (honey dipper) and confirmed it in a passage ('honey dippers'). It answered with the bare partner word.

patch.reasoning: Most successes came from rules already in the skill: verbatim archive copying, anchor to owner, and ignoring filler. Two small gaps remain. First, the strategic type-check could push the agent to reject an archived pun answer, so Rule 3 should say explicitly that the archive answer and its category header beat the type-check. Second, 'seen here ... used with this X' clues with no image have no explicit procedure, and the collocation-matching that worked deserves one line. Both edits are additive and keyed to visible clue features, so they should not disturb the stable passes. I am not proposing another global answer-line template, since several earlier templates were rejected.

edits.target: - Archive lines may also be formatted 'CATEGORY | clue text | answer'. Take the answer that follows the clue, even if the whole context is one short passage.
edits.content: - The archive answer and its CATEGORY header beat the slot-type check. A pun or idiom answer is correct even if it does not look like the clue's noun ('W. has this type of job' under WEATHER WORDS & PHRASES -> 'high pressure'). Do not swap in a literal job title. Stage directions and audio or video links inside the archived clue are noise, so match on the factual words.

edits.target: - Honor qualifiers when the context offers several names for the same thing: 'Greek god of erotic love' -> 'Eros' (not Roman 'Cupid').
edits.content: - 'X seen here / shown here is used with this <category>' (the picture is missing): the clue names an object and asks for its standard partner. Search the passages for the object word next to a candidate of the stated category ('honey dippers', 'honey dipper' -> 'honey' for 'sticky substance'). Answer with the bare partner word, without the object word, and without a looser member of the category that never appears paired with the object.
